clue.text: One beau in the sack, which is no place for a 24

definitions.text: which is no place for a 24

indicators.note: in places the one-and-beau pair inside the word for the sack

parts.note: getting the chop means being sacked
one is the Roman numeral I
Beau Nash was the famous Regency dandy of Bath

explanation.surface: A lone suitor ends up in bed, somewhere a bull should never be let loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is BULL, so the definition points to the proverbial bull in a china shop; 'sack' invites thoughts of bed, but here it means dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull in a china shop is the idiom for clumsy destruction, so such a shop is the last place for one.

clue.text: Firms need a drink

parts.note: two firms, each abbreviated CO for company

explanation.surface: Businesses require a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chocolate beverage made from cacao powder is a familiar drink.

clue.text: Inability to change into £10 in coppers

indicators.note: into puts the changed short word inside the money phrase

parts.note: ten pounds is a thousand pence: I M (one thousand) PENCE

indicators.note: change asks for the two letters of to to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cannot swap their tenner for a pile of copper coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' gives OT, which goes 'into' I M PENCE: one thousand (M) pence makes £10 in copper coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Powerlessness or lack of ability is the general sense of this word, beyond its sexual one.

clue.text: One out of three sisters — one out of nine, with brother — in stake

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the word for a stake

parts.note: an ante is the stake in poker

indicators.note: one out of tells us to remove the letter for one, I, from the number word

explanation.surface: One of the three Brontë sisters is compared with one of the nine Muses, plus a brother, at stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one out of' takes I from NINE, leaving NNE; NNE and BRO go 'in' ANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngest Brontë, author of Agnes Grey, was one of three literary sisters.

clue.text: Not a single loo in the house? Explain!

indicators.note: in places the loo pieces inside the word for house

parts.note: a house is a home
WC, water closet, is a loo
not a single one is nought, the letter O

explanation.surface: A visitor is baffled to find no toilet anywhere in the house and demands an explanation.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking why something is so is a demand to explain it, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Moody and irritable with an appeal to be signed when heard

indicators.note: with an says the answer plus the letters an makes the sound of the appeal
when heard means the appeal is judged by its sound not its spelling

parts.note: a petition is an appeal that people sign

explanation.surface: A sulky, grumpy person is asked to add their name to an appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer 'with an' added, said aloud, sounds like PETITION ('when heard'), so the answer is that sound less AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Peevish and sulky in a childish way is exactly this word's meaning.

clue.text: 3's sister to see about road

indicators.note: about means the see's letters go round the road

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see
the M1, read as MI, is a British motorway

explanation.surface: Anne's sister is sent to visit a church about a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is ANNE BRONTE. The M1 is the London–Leeds motorway, written MI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Brontë's elder sister was the author of the Yorkshire moorland novel.

clue.text: Garden, English part of

indicators.note: part of means only some letters of the word garden are used, its last three

explanation.surface: A garden is described as part of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' takes DEN from the end of 'Garden', with E for English before it; the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical paradise of Adam and Eve is the original garden.

clue.text: Murdoch with her last lucky lot

parts.note: Iris Murdoch was the ...-born novelist

indicators.note: last means take only the final letter of the word with

explanation.surface: The novelist Iris Murdoch is joined by her final fortunate group.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter means H as 'her last', Murdoch's last letter; the final letter of 'with' is the same H.
explanation.definitionFit: The luck of the Irish is a stock phrase, so the people of Ireland are the proverbial lucky lot.

clue.text: Ash covering all good day girls that repent

indicators.note: girls that repent change their ways, so these letters change their order

explanation.surface: An ash tree spreads over all the schoolgirls who are sorry for their sins.
explanation.walkthrough: G plus DAYGIRLS rearranged gives the Norse world-tree.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth the world tree is a vast ash whose branches spread over every realm.

clue.text: Bird that's covered

definitions.meaning: a castrated cockerel fattened for eating
with a ..., so covered over or capped

explanation.definitionFit: A castrated cock bird is a farmyard fowl; read in two words it describes something wearing a hat.

clue.text: Welsh boy backs surrounding Wagner's work with 8's, which is 28's

indicators.note: surrounding means the reversed name goes round Wagner's work
backs means the Welsh name is read from right to left

parts.note: Huw is a Welsh boy's name
The Ring is Wagner's operatic cycle
the figure 8 written as a word, made plural

explanation.surface: A Welsh lad reverses round Wagner's opera cycle with an ash tree's work, credited to a pen name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' turns HUW into WUH, which goes 'surrounding' THE RING. '8's' tempts the solver towards the ash tree at 8, but it means EIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellis Bell was the pseudonym under which Emily Brontë published her only novel, so it is that writer's book.

clue.text: Drug makes insect very stupid — should be born, not died

parts.note: an ant is an insect

indicators.note: born and died are the genealogy abbreviations B and D, so one letter swaps for the other

parts.note: idiotic means very stupid

explanation.surface: A medicine turns a bug into a complete fool, but birth should replace death.
explanation.walkthrough: IDIOTIC with its D (died) swapped for B (born) gives IBIOTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Penicillin is the classic example of this kind of drug, which kills bacteria.

clue.text: Deity in authority

indicators.note: in shows the god's name sits inside the word authority

explanation.surface: A god holds power.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse god of thunder is a deity.

clue.text: Some fighting forces retain numbers for boxing

indicators.note: some means only part of the word fighting, its first two letters
retain means the forcing word holds the numbers inside it

parts.note: stuffs means forces or crams
IC is 99 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Part of the fighting is done by armed forces who keep the numbers up through boxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighting forces' reads as the army, but 'forces' is the verb STUFFS, which IC goes into.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting with the fists is boxing, in an old-fashioned word.

clue.text: Comfort for the organist?

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to soothe someone in distress
the keyboard and stop desk an organ is played from

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to soothe as a verb and, as a noun, the keyboard unit of an organ.

clue.text: 3's sister's not a good girl and the rest turn up to keep her

indicators.note: to keep means the reversed letters hold the girl inside them
turn up in a down clue reads the letters from the bottom upwards

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and the rest
a harlot is a woman of bad reputation

explanation.surface: A Brontë sister is no nice girl, and the others show up to protect her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses the abbreviation, giving CTE, which goes round the girl ('to keep'). 3 is ANNE BRONTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The eldest surviving Brontë, author of Jane Eyre, was Anne's sister.

clue.text: See 10
Wild urchin are causing a storm

indicators.note: wild means the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Unruly street children are kicking up a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical cyclone of the Atlantic is a violent storm.

clue.text: A month in charge of pre-empting 11?

parts.note: Sept is the abbreviation for September

explanation.surface: A month spent in control heads off the need for medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is ANTIBIOTIC: keeping things germ-free removes the need for such a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile and germ-free conditions prevent infection, so the drug is never needed.

clue.text: Is inclined to enter church to achieve purification

indicators.note: to enter means the leaning word goes inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
leans means is inclined

explanation.surface: Someone tilts into a church in search of spiritual purity.
explanation.definitionFit: To make clean or pure is to bring about purification.

clue.text: White note is not legitimate

definitions.meaning: a note that is neither sharp nor flat, played on a white piano key
an old term for a child born outside marriage

explanation.definitionFit: The white keys of a piano play unaltered notes, and a child born out of wedlock was once called this.

clue.text: Game or its object?

parts.note: the name of the sport read as two words describes what players aim to do with the ball

explanation.definitionFit: A team sport whose aim is to put a ball through a raised net; split, its name states that aim.

clue.text: Security to change levels?

definitions.meaning: a fastening that keeps a door secure
a canal chamber that raises or lowers boats between water levels

explanation.definitionFit: A fastening device gives security, and the canal device of that name moves boats between heights.

clue.text: Place reserved to accommodate deity

indicators.note: to accommodate shows the two words hold the goddess's name inside them

explanation.surface: A seat is kept for a god.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman goddess of agriculture is a deity.

clue.text: Open land and seaside feature in 10 15

parts.note: a heath is open uncultivated land
a cliff is a feature of the coast

explanation.surface: Moorland and coastal rock appear in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 15 is the Brontë novel, whose brooding hero this is.
explanation.definitionFit: The brooding hero of Emily Brontë's novel is a character in it.

clue.text: Cuban field marshal?

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange, so the letters of field are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A Cuban military officer of the highest rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'field marshal' looks like one military rank, but 'marshal' is the verb arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Castro, the Cuban revolutionary leader, is known by this first name.

clue.text: Optimistic beast?

definitions.meaning: on the stock market, one who expects prices to rise

explanation.definitionFit: A stock-market optimist expecting prices to rise has this name, as does the male of cattle.

clue.text: One of five, the first, in Scarlett's home, a town near Rome

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside Scarlett's home

parts.note: Tara is Scarlett O'Hara's plantation in Gone with the Wind
a quin is one of quintuplets
I is the Roman numeral one, the first

explanation.surface: A quintuplet, the firstborn, lives on Scarlett O'Hara's estate in an Italian town.
explanation.definitionFit: This Etruscan town in Lazio lies north-west of Rome.

clue.text: German lady reveals her country's wrongdoing

parts.note: Frau is German for a married woman
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A German woman exposes her nation's misdeeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Deception for gain is a form of criminal wrongdoing.

clue.text: Stand what one can stand at and live

parts.note: soldiers stand at ease
L is the abbreviation for live, as on electrical wiring

explanation.surface: A soldier's posture and life itself are offered as something to stand on.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's frame for holding a canvas is a stand.

clue.text: 6 across is second among measures

indicators.note: among means the short word and the letter go between the two measures

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth, so two of them
B is second in the alphabet

explanation.surface: Emily is rated second among the standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 across is EMILY Brontë, who published under this male pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Brontë published her novel under this male pseudonym.
